records.name: 2023 BC Q1(a): interpret a definite integral of a flow rate and approximate it with a right Riemann sum
records.description: A differentiable flow rate is tabulated at six unequally spaced times in seconds, in gallons per second. The part asks for a sentence giving the meaning of the definite integral of that rate over a stated time window, with units, and then for a right Riemann sum over three named subintervals as an approximation of the same integral.
records.anchor_quote: A customer at a gas station is pumping gasoline into a gas tank
scoring_behaviors: Interpretation point earned only when the response names gallons of gasoline added or pumped and the time interval from 60 to 135 seconds (sg-23:2).
Form point earned when at least five of the six factors of the three-term sum are correct (sg-23:2).
Answer point lost for any error in the sum; a fully correct left Riemann sum earns one of the last two points, and an unsupported value of the sum earns neither (sg-23:2, sg-23:3).
records.notation_requirements: Integral notation with limits is supplied by the stem; the response must show products of a tabulated rate value and a subinterval width, and units of gallons attached to the interpretation.
records.justification_requirements: No theorem justification. The interpretation must name the quantity, its units, and the interval.
records.difficulty_notes: Two concepts combined in one part, an interpretation and a numerical approximation, each scored separately; nonuniform subinterval widths; table representation converted to a verbal statement and to a sum; units carry their own scoring weight.
diagnostic_distinctions: Correct sum but interpretation missing units or interval: language failure, not approximation failure.
Left endpoints used throughout: endpoint convention not read from the prompt, not an arithmetic failure.
Correct products but widths taken as equal: the nonuniform partition was not noticed.
Unsupported numerical value only: the sum was done on the calculator and the required structure was never written.

records.name: 2023 BC Q1(b): decide whether the Mean Value Theorem forces a zero of the derivative
records.description: Using the same tabulated differentiable rate, the part asks whether a point must exist strictly inside a stated subinterval at which the derivative of the rate is zero, and asks for a justification.
records.anchor_quote: A customer at a gas station is pumping gasoline into a gas tank
scoring_behaviors: First point earned by presenting equal endpoint values or their difference as zero, in any of three accepted forms (sg-23:3).
Second point requires the first point, a statement that the rate is continuous because it is differentiable, and an affirmative answer (sg-23:3).
Either the Mean Value Theorem or Rolle's Theorem may be named; a response that names the Intermediate Value Theorem cannot earn the second point (sg-23:3).
records.notation_requirements: Function notation at the two endpoints, and prime notation for the derivative whose zero is claimed.
records.justification_requirements: Continuity must be deduced from the stated differentiability, the equal endpoint values must be exhibited, and the named theorem must be the correct one.
records.difficulty_notes: Theorem recognition under a table representation; a hypothesis that must be derived rather than read off; a common competing theorem that scores zero; two concepts combined, differentiability implying continuity and the Mean Value Theorem.
diagnostic_distinctions: Yes with no endpoint computation: the conclusion was guessed from the shape of the table.
Intermediate Value Theorem cited: the target of the theorem was taken to be a function value rather than a derivative value.
Continuity asserted without deriving it from differentiability: the hypothesis chain was not tracked.

records.name: 2023 BC Q1(c): average value of a modelled flow rate over an interval
records.description: A closed-form model for the same flow rate is supplied. The part asks for the average rate of flow over the whole time interval and requires the setup for the calculation to be shown.
records.anchor_quote: A customer at a gas station is pumping gasoline into a gas tank
scoring_behaviors: Average value formula point earned for the integral divided by the interval length, in one step or several (sg-23:3).
Answer point earned for the decimal value; an incomplete multi-step presentation that equates the integral to the average earns one of two points (sg-23:4).
A bare definite integral set equal to the average value earns neither point, and a degree-mode answer loses the first point it would otherwise have earned (sg-23:4).
records.notation_requirements: Average value written as a definite integral divided by the interval length, in standard notation rather than calculator syntax.
records.justification_requirements: None beyond showing the setup.
records.difficulty_notes: Calculator workflow with a required written setup; average value confused with average rate of change; radian mode dependency; single concept but strict communication rules.
diagnostic_distinctions: Integral value reported without dividing: average value formula not recalled.
Answer matching the degree-mode value: calculator mode error, not a calculus failure.
Correct value with the integral equated to it: communication failure that costs the setup point only.

records.name: 2023 BC Q1(d): value and contextual meaning of the derivative of the flow model
records.description: Using the same closed-form model, the part asks for the value of the derivative of the rate at a stated time and for an interpretation of that value in the situation described.
records.anchor_quote: A customer at a gas station is pumping gasoline into a gas tank
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for a numerical value of the derivative, which may appear only inside the interpretation (sg-23:4).
Second point requires some declared numerical value and an interpretation carrying both the rate-of-a-rate phrasing and the time at which it holds (sg-23:4).
An interpretation phrased as decreasing at a rate of a negative number, or increasing at a rate of the positive magnitude, does not earn the second point (sg-23:4).
records.notation_requirements: Prime notation on the model function, and compound units of gallons per second per second in the interpretation.
records.justification_requirements: None; the interpretation itself carries the second point and must be self-consistent in sign.
records.difficulty_notes: Rate of a rate interpretation; sign and magnitude must agree in words; calculator derivative at a point; context vocabulary must avoid motion language.
diagnostic_distinctions: Correct value with the sign restated inside the word decreasing: double negation, a language failure.
Value interpreted as an amount rather than a rate: the order of the derivative was lost.
Acceleration or velocity vocabulary used: the non-motion context was not respected.

records.name: 2023 BC Q2(a): acceleration vector of a particle on a plane curve
records.description: A particle moves on a plane curve with one coordinate given explicitly as a function of time, the derivative of the other supplied, and the position given at an initial time. The part asks for the acceleration vector at a stated time with the setup shown.
records.anchor_quote: a particle is moving along the curve shown so that its position at time
scoring_behaviors: One point for the second derivative of each coordinate presented with its setup (sg-23:5).
A correct symbolic pair with a missing or incorrect evaluation earns one of the two points, as does an unsupported correct vector (sg-23:5, sg-23:6).
A response that equates a symbolic expression directly to a numerical pair earns only one point; components may be listed separately if labelled (sg-23:6).
records.notation_requirements: Vector or ordered pair notation with labelled components, and second derivative notation for each coordinate.
records.justification_requirements: None beyond showing the setup for each component.
records.difficulty_notes: Chain rule on an exponential of a trigonometric argument; one coordinate supplied only through its derivative, so the orders of differentiation differ between components; calculator evaluation with a required written setup.
diagnostic_distinctions: Velocity vector reported: the order of differentiation was misread for both components.
One component differentiated once and the other twice: the asymmetric givens were not tracked.
Unsupported correct vector: calculator use without the required setup.

records.name: 2023 BC Q2(b): first time at which the speed of the particle reaches a stated value
records.description: For the same planar motion, the part asks for the earliest time in a closed interval at which the speed equals a given number, with the work leading to the answer shown.
records.anchor_quote: a particle is moving along the curve shown so that its position at time
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for the speed equation, explicitly or by implication; the phrase speed equals the value alone does not earn it (sg-23:6).
Second point earned for the earliest solution; the response need not mention the later solution, and an unsupported time earns neither point (sg-23:6).
A parenthesis error inside either squared component loses the first point but not the second (sg-23:6).
records.notation_requirements: Speed written as the square root of the sum of squared coordinate derivatives, with parentheses that keep each component squared as a whole.
records.justification_requirements: None; the equation set equal to the given speed carries the reasoning.
records.difficulty_notes: Speed as a magnitude assembled from two derivatives; calculator equation solve on an interval with two roots; parenthesis discipline explicitly scored.
diagnostic_distinctions: The later root reported: the word first was not acted on.
Sum of derivatives instead of the root of the sum of squares: magnitude concept missing.
Missing parentheses inside a squared exponential: notation failure that still permits the correct value.

records.name: 2023 BC Q2(c): tangent slope to the path and the x-coordinate recovered from a rate
records.description: For the same motion the part asks for the slope of the tangent to the path at a stated time and, separately, for the x-coordinate of the position at that time, given only the derivative of that coordinate and the initial position.
records.anchor_quote: a particle is moving along the curve shown so that its position at time
scoring_behaviors: First point requires communicating the slope as the quotient of the two time derivatives, in any of four accepted forms, and an incorrect component derivative may be imported from the earlier part if it was declared there (sg-23:7).
Second point earned for the definite integral of the x-derivative, with or without the initial condition and with or without the differential (sg-23:7, sg-23:8).
Third point is lost when the final statement is mathematically incorrect, for example when the integral alone is equated to the coordinate value that includes the initial condition (sg-23:8).
records.notation_requirements: Quotient of Leibniz derivatives for the slope, and an accumulation expression with the initial value added to a definite integral for the coordinate.
records.justification_requirements: None; the structure of the quotient and of the accumulation expression carries the points.
records.difficulty_notes: Two distinct tasks in one part with three points; a coordinate available only as an accumulation; multi-step dependency on the earlier part; calculator integration with a required setup.
diagnostic_distinctions: Slope reported as the x-derivative over the y-derivative: the quotient was inverted.
Coordinate reported as the integral alone: the initial condition was dropped.
Integral written without limits: the accumulation was treated as an antiderivative.

records.name: 2023 BC Q2(d): total distance travelled by the particle over an interval
records.description: For the same motion the part asks for the total distance travelled over the full time interval, with the setup for the calculation shown.
records.anchor_quote: a particle is moving along the curve shown so that its position at time
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for the correct integrand inside a definite integral over the stated interval (sg-23:8).
Parenthesis errors already assessed in the speed part do not affect scoring here (sg-23:8).
An incorrect speed integrand imported from the earlier part still earns the first point but forfeits the answer point, and an unsupported value earns neither point (sg-23:8).
records.notation_requirements: Definite integral of the speed with numerical limits, written in standard notation.
records.justification_requirements: None beyond showing the setup.
records.difficulty_notes: Arc length integrand reused from the speed work; calculator evaluation; import rules that make the part partially dependent on the earlier speed part.
diagnostic_distinctions: Displacement components integrated separately: total distance confused with net change.
Correct integral with a wrong value: calculator entry or mode failure rather than a set-up failure.
Unsupported value: setup requirement ignored.

records.name: 2023 BC Q3(a): sketch the solution curve through a given point on a slope field
records.description: A slope field for a first-order differential equation modelling a warming temperature is printed. The part asks for the solution curve through the stated initial point to be sketched on that field.
records.anchor_quote: A bottle of milk is taken out of a refrigerator and placed in a pan of hot water
scoring_behaviors: The single point requires a curve through the stated point that reaches reasonably close to both side edges of the printed rectangle and conflicts with none of the drawn slope segments (sg-23:9).
Only the portion of the curve inside the printed field is considered (sg-23:9).
The curve must lie entirely below the horizontal segments at the equilibrium level (sg-23:9).
records.notation_requirements: Graphical only; no symbolic requirement.
records.justification_requirements: None.
records.difficulty_notes: Single concept, graphical production rather than computation; the equilibrium level is an unstated boundary that the sketch must respect; no calculator.
diagnostic_distinctions: Curve crossing the equilibrium level: the bound on the solution given in the stem was not used.
Curve stopping short of the edges: the field was read locally rather than as a whole.
Curve through the wrong point: the initial condition was misread.

records.name: 2023 BC Q3(b): tangent line approximation of a temperature two minutes later
records.description: For the same differential equation and initial temperature, the part asks for the tangent line at the initial time to be used to approximate the temperature two minutes later.
records.anchor_quote: A bottle of milk is taken out of a refrigerator and placed in a pan of hot water
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for the derivative value at the initial time, which may appear inside a tangent line equation or inside the approximation (sg-23:10).
Second point requires an approximation built from a tangent line through the initial point whose slope is the declared derivative value; an unsupported approximation does not earn it (sg-23:10).
The approximation need not be simplified, but an incorrect simplification forfeits the second point (sg-23:10).
records.notation_requirements: Leibniz derivative evaluated at the initial time, and a point-slope tangent line or an equivalent increment expression.
records.justification_requirements: None.
records.difficulty_notes: Slope obtained from the differential equation rather than from a formula for the function; two concepts combined, local linearity and the differential equation; no calculator arithmetic.
diagnostic_distinctions: Differential equation evaluated at the target time instead of the initial time: the tangency point was misplaced.
Initial value used as the slope: the roles of the value and the rate were exchanged.
Correct slope with an arithmetic slip: computation failure, not a linearisation failure.

records.name: 2023 BC Q3(c): second derivative in terms of the quantity and the direction of the approximation error
records.description: The part asks for an expression for the second derivative of the temperature in terms of the temperature itself, and then for that expression to be used to decide whether the earlier tangent line approximation is an underestimate or an overestimate, with a reason.
records.anchor_quote: A bottle of milk is taken out of a refrigerator and placed in a pan of hot water
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for either accepted form of the second derivative in terms of the quantity; a later simplification error forfeits the second point (sg-23:11).
An expression left in terms of the first derivative does not earn the first point but stays eligible for the second (sg-23:11).

Second point requires a sign statement about the second derivative, or a decreasing first derivative, or concavity, together with the overestimate conclusion; an argument resting on a single point does not earn it (sg-23:11).
records.notation_requirements: Second derivative in Leibniz notation expressed in the dependent variable, and an explicit sign or concavity statement.
records.justification_requirements: The direction of the error must be tied to the sign of the second derivative across the interval, not at one point.
records.difficulty_notes: Chain rule applied to a differential equation; the bound on the quantity given in the stem must be reused to fix a sign; conclusion depends on the earlier part; justification scored separately from the expression.
diagnostic_distinctions: Second derivative left in terms of the first derivative: substitution back into the differential equation was not carried out.
Concavity argued at the initial point only: the interval-wide requirement was missed.
Correct concavity with the wrong conclusion: the relationship between concavity and tangent line position was inverted.

records.name: 2023 BC Q3(d): particular solution by separation of variables
records.description: The part asks for the particular solution of the same differential equation with the stated initial temperature, obtained by separation of variables.
records.anchor_quote: A bottle of milk is taken out of a refrigerator and placed in a pan of hot water
scoring_behaviors: A response with no separation of variables earns none of the four points (sg-23:12).
An antiderivative written without absolute value symbols stays eligible for all four points, and a response with no constant of integration can earn at most the first two (sg-23:12).

The third point requires the first two and is earned by placing the constant in an equation and substituting the initial pair; the fourth requires the first three and is earned only for the stated closed form (sg-23:12).
records.notation_requirements: Separated differentials on opposite sides, a logarithm of the shifted quantity, a single constant of integration, and an exponential form solved for the quantity.
records.justification_requirements: The sign of the absolute value must be resolved consistently with the bound stated in the stem.
records.difficulty_notes: Four-point chain with strict eligibility gating; logarithm and exponential algebra; absolute value branch selection; prerequisite depth in logarithm rules; no calculator.
diagnostic_distinctions: Separation correct but constant added after exponentiating: the constant was attached at the wrong stage.
Absolute value resolved with the wrong sign: the stated bound on the quantity was not used.
General solution left unsolved for the quantity: the final algebraic step was omitted, which costs only the last point.
No separation at all: the method named in the prompt was not attempted, which costs the whole part.

records.name: 2023 BC Q4(a): classify a candidate point from the behaviour of the derivative graph
records.description: The graph of the derivative of a function, built from two line segments and a semicircle, is supplied along with one function value. The part asks whether the function has a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at a stated input, with a reason.
records.anchor_quote: The function f is defined on the closed interval
scoring_behaviors: Declaring that the derivative does not change sign at the stated input, and concluding neither, is sufficient for the point (sg-23:13).
Intervals of positivity need not be presented, but any presented interval must be correct, with endpoints optional (sg-23:13).
Declaring the derivative positive before and after the input, without saying that the sign does not change, does not earn the point (sg-23:13).
records.notation_requirements: Prime notation naming the derivative explicitly rather than an unnamed referent.
records.justification_requirements: The reason must be a statement about the sign change of the derivative, and the subject of that statement must be named.
records.difficulty_notes: Single concept but a strict wording rule; graphical representation with a zero of the derivative that is not an extremum; the classification hinges on recognising a touching zero.
diagnostic_distinctions: Relative minimum claimed: a zero of the derivative was assumed to be an extremum.
Correct conclusion with positive before and after phrasing: the sign-change criterion was not stated.
Reason given about the function rather than the derivative: vague or misdirected referent.

records.name: 2023 BC Q4(b): open intervals on which the graph is concave down
records.description: From the same derivative graph, the part asks on which open intervals the graph of the function is concave down, with a reason.
records.anchor_quote: The function f is defined on the closed interval
scoring_behaviors: Interval point earned only for both correct intervals, with either or both endpoints permitted (sg-23:14).
The interval point must be earned before the reason point is available (sg-23:14).
Reason point requires a correct discussion of the derivative decreasing or of the slopes of the derivative graph; exactly one correct interval with a correct reason scores one of two (sg-23:14).
records.notation_requirements: Interval notation, and a named derivative as the subject of the reason.
records.justification_requirements: Concavity must be tied to the derivative decreasing, read from the supplied graph.
records.difficulty_notes: Two disjoint intervals must both be found; reading concavity from a derivative graph rather than a second derivative; gating of the reason point behind the interval point.
diagnostic_distinctions: One interval found: the semicircular arc or a segment was skipped.
Intervals of negative derivative given: concavity confused with decrease.
Correct intervals with a reason about the function decreasing: the wrong derivative order was used.

records.name: 2023 BC Q4(c): limit of an indeterminate quotient using L'Hospital's Rule
records.description: The part asks for the value of a limit whose numerator involves the function and whose denominator is a quadratic vanishing at the same input, or a demonstration that no limit exists, with justification.
records.anchor_quote: The function f is defined on the closed interval
scoring_behaviors: First point earned by presenting the two limits, numerator and denominator, separately; a limit written explicitly as zero over zero does not earn it (sg-23:14).
Second point earned by applying the rule, shown by at least one correct derivative inside a limit of a ratio of derivatives (sg-23:14).
Third point earned for the correct value with supporting work (sg-23:14).
records.notation_requirements: Limit notation carried through every line, prime notation for the differentiated numerator, and the value of the function at the point obtained from continuity.
records.justification_requirements: The indeterminate form must be established by separate limits before the rule is invoked, and continuity must be drawn from differentiability to evaluate the numerator.
records.difficulty_notes: Three concepts combined, differentiability implying continuity, the indeterminate form, and the rule itself; a function value read from the stem and a derivative value read from a graph; notation discipline on limits is explicitly scored.
diagnostic_distinctions: Rule applied without exhibiting the two limits: the hypothesis was assumed rather than verified.
Zero over zero written as an equation: notation failure that costs only the first point.
Whole quotient differentiated: the rule was confused with the quotient rule.
Derivative value misread from the graph: representation failure, not a rule failure.

records.name: 2023 BC Q4(d): absolute minimum value on a closed interval by the candidates test
records.description: The part asks for the absolute minimum value of the function on the whole closed interval on which it is defined, with justification, given the derivative graph and one function value.
records.anchor_quote: The function f is defined on the closed interval
scoring_behaviors: First point requires stating that the derivative is set equal to zero; merely listing its zeros is not sufficient (sg-23:15).
Any error in evaluating the function at a critical point or endpoint forfeits the justification point, and a response that ignores either endpoint does not earn it (sg-23:15).
Some candidate values may be omitted if the corresponding input is eliminated by an argument, and the answer point is earned only for the minimum value, not for its location (sg-23:15).
records.notation_requirements: A candidates table or equivalent list, with function values obtained by accumulating signed areas from the derivative graph.
records.justification_requirements: A global argument over all candidates, or an elimination argument, is required; a local test alone is insufficient.
records.difficulty_notes: Function values must be built by accumulating areas under the derivative graph including a semicircular region; several concepts combined; the answer point distinguishes the value from its location; every arithmetic slip is punished in the justification point.
diagnostic_distinctions: Location reported instead of the value: the question asked for a value.
Endpoints omitted: the candidates test was truncated to a first derivative test.
Semicircular area miscomputed: geometry failure, not a candidates test failure.
Zeros listed without setting the derivative to zero: the criterion was implied rather than stated.

records.name: 2023 BC Q5(a): area of a region enclosed by two graphs with one integral supplied
records.description: Two graphs are shown on a closed interval, one given by a formula and the other left unspecified except for one value and the value of its definite integral over the interval. The part asks for the area of the shaded region enclosed by the two graphs.
records.anchor_quote: The graphs of the functions f and g are shown in the figure
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for any of four accepted difference integrands inside a definite integral; incorrect limits forfeit the third point (sg-23:16).
Second point earned for the logarithmic antiderivative of the given function in either accepted form (sg-23:17).
Third point requires the first two and the correct value; incorrect substitution limits after a change of variable, or an incorrect final statement, forfeit it (sg-23:17).
records.notation_requirements: Difference of the two functions inside a definite integral with correct limits, and a logarithmic antiderivative with the argument shifted.
records.justification_requirements: None; the structure of the integrand and the arithmetic carry the points.
records.difficulty_notes: One of the two integrals is supplied as a number, so the part combines a property of definite integrals with an antidifferentiation; logarithm antiderivative with an inner shift; no calculator.
diagnostic_distinctions: Order of subtraction reversed with a positive answer forced: the upper curve was not identified.
Supplied integral value ignored and the unspecified function integrated symbolically: the given data were not used.
Limits not converted during substitution: substitution bookkeeping failure.
Correct integral with a sign slip in the logarithm difference: arithmetic failure.

records.name: 2023 BC Q5(b): evaluate an improper integral of a squared rational function
records.description: The part asks for the value of an improper integral with an infinite upper limit whose integrand is the square of the supplied rational function, or for a demonstration that it diverges.
records.anchor_quote: The graphs of the functions f and g are shown in the figure
scoring_behaviors: First point requires correct limit notation throughout, with no arithmetic performed on infinity (sg-23:17).
Second point earned for an antiderivative of the correct reciprocal shape with a positive constant, with or without correct limit notation; a wrong constant forfeits the third point (sg-23:17).
Third point earned only for the stated value, and incorrect substitution limits forfeit it (sg-23:17).
records.notation_requirements: An upper limit replaced by a parameter with an explicit limit as that parameter grows without bound, carried through every line.
records.justification_requirements: Convergence is established by the limit calculation itself; the improperness must be handled by notation rather than by substituting infinity.
records.difficulty_notes: Notation discipline is one of three points; power rule on a negative exponent after squaring; end behaviour limit; no calculator.
diagnostic_distinctions: Infinity substituted directly: improperness recognised but handled without limit notation.
Integrand squared incorrectly, leaving the first power: algebra failure before any calculus.
Antiderivative constant wrong: the chain factor from the inner shift was dropped.
Correct antiderivative with limits unconverted after substitution: bookkeeping failure.

records.name: 2023 BC Q5(c): definite integral of a product involving an unknown derivative by parts
records.description: A new function is defined as the identity times the derivative of the unspecified function. The part asks for the value of its definite integral over the stated interval, using the value of the function at the right endpoint and the supplied value of its integral.
records.anchor_quote: The graphs of the functions f and g are shown in the figure
scoring_behaviors: First and second points may be earned with the choice of parts left implicit, provided the parts expression appears (sg-23:18).
Limits of integration may be present, absent, or partly present in the work for the first two points, and the tabular layout is accepted (sg-23:18).
Third point is earned only for the correct value and only if the first two points were earned (sg-23:18).
records.notation_requirements: An explicit or implied choice of the two factors, the parts expression with the boundary term evaluated, and the supplied integral value substituted.
records.justification_requirements: None; the structure of the parts expression carries the reasoning.
records.difficulty_notes: Integration by parts where one factor is an unknown function supplied only through two data values; three concepts combined; eligibility gating on the answer point; no calculator.
diagnostic_distinctions: Parts applied with the factors exchanged: the choice rule was not applied to the unknown derivative.
Boundary term omitted: the definite form of the parts expression was not used.
Supplied integral value ignored: the given data were not connected to the remaining integral.
Correct structure with a sign error on the boundary term: arithmetic failure that costs only the answer point.

records.name: 2023 BC Q6(a): fourth derivative from a given relation and the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial
records.description: A function is specified by two initial derivative values and by relations giving its second and third derivatives in terms of itself and its first derivative. The part asks for the fourth derivative and for the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial about the origin, with the work shown.
records.anchor_quote: The function f has derivatives of all orders for all real numbers
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for a correct fourth derivative or for the correct product rule structure applied to the supplied third derivative (sg-23:19).
Second point earned only for a completely correct expression for the fourth derivative (sg-23:19).
A response that earns the first but not the second may still use a consistent nonzero value for the fourth-degree coefficient (sg-23:19).
A polynomial carrying a nonzero third-degree term, any term above degree four, or trailing dots does not earn the last point (sg-23:19).
records.notation_requirements: Higher-order derivative notation, factorial denominators in the polynomial coefficients, and a polynomial written without trailing dots.
records.justification_requirements: None; the differentiation chain must be visible.
records.difficulty_notes: Product rule and chain rule combined inside a supplied derivative relation; four points with a coefficient chain; one coefficient vanishes so the polynomial has a gap; factorial bookkeeping; no calculator.
diagnostic_distinctions: Product rule missing on the supplied third derivative: the structure of the relation was not recognised.
Derivative values correct but factorials omitted: the polynomial coefficient rule was not applied.
Third-degree term written as nonzero: a vanishing derivative value was not carried through.
Trailing dots appended: the polynomial was confused with the series.

records.name: 2023 BC Q6(b): Lagrange error bound with a supplied derivative bound
records.description: Given a bound on the fifth derivative on a stated interval, the part asks for the Lagrange error bound to be used to show that the fourth-degree approximation at a stated input is within a given tolerance.
records.anchor_quote: The function f has derivatives of all orders for all real numbers
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for the bound written with the maximum of the next derivative over the interval, or for the numerical form obtained from the supplied bound; a later simplification error forfeits the second point (sg-23:20).
Second point requires communicating an inequality chain from the bound down to the stated tolerance (sg-23:20).
A response that states the error equals the bound, rather than is at most the bound, does not earn the second point (sg-23:20).
records.notation_requirements: Factorial denominator of order one above the polynomial degree, the increment raised to that order, and inequality symbols rather than equality.
records.justification_requirements: The inequality must be explicit and must terminate at the stated tolerance.
records.difficulty_notes: A show-that prompt where the final number is given, so all credit rests on structure; inequality discipline explicitly scored; factorial and power bookkeeping; no calculator.
diagnostic_distinctions: Degree used in the factorial instead of one more: the order of the bound was misread.
Equality asserted instead of an inequality: the bound was treated as the error.
Bound written but never compared with the tolerance: the show-that instruction was not completed.

records.name: 2023 BC Q6(c): second-degree Taylor polynomial for a function defined through a derivative relation
records.description: A second function is defined by one value and by a derivative equal to an exponential times the original function. The part asks for the second-degree Taylor polynomial of that second function about the origin.
records.anchor_quote: The function f has derivatives of all orders for all real numbers
scoring_behaviors: First point earned for the product rule applied to the defining derivative, or for its evaluation at the centre (sg-23:20).
Second point earned for a polynomial whose first two terms are correct, with or without supporting work (sg-23:20).
Third point requires support for the quadratic coefficient; a polynomial with terms above degree two, or with trailing dots, does not earn it (sg-23:20, sg-23:21).
An alternate route through the known exponential series is accepted, with the three points reassigned to the product series, two correct terms, and the complete polynomial (sg-23:21).
records.notation_requirements: Product rule on an exponential times an unspecified function, a factorial denominator on the quadratic term, and no trailing dots.
records.justification_requirements: None, but the quadratic coefficient must be supported.
records.difficulty_notes: Second function defined only through its derivative, so values must be chained from the first function; two acceptable solution routes; factorial bookkeeping; no calculator.
